beats.intent: The image moves through a dense encoder, window partitioning, repeated shared DQ-CTM ticks, and a decoder.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method keeps dense image information available while a compact thought process works on it. The encoder builds the feature carrier from the low-resolution input. Windowing turns that carrier into token groups without discarding the spatial field. The DQ-CTM stage repeats its thought ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense carrier back into the super-resolved output.

params.headline: ThinkSR keeps dense output while compact thought repeats

beats.intent: The carrier equation first encodes the low-resolution image as dense features, then partitions those features into windows that keep every token.
beats.narration: The carrier is defined before the compact process starts reading it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into a dense feature field. The window operator partitions that field into tokens while keeping the carrier intact.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first and windowed second

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the cheapest method in the benchmark; its 1.129 million parameters are the second largest of the five.
beats.narration: Parameter count is a cost, and the benchmark does not make ThinkSR look especially small. CATANet is the smallest reported model at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN and IMDN are still below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is the largest reported model at 1.592 million parameters.
